ai.summary: A global AI infrastructure boom is driving heavy investment in advanced chip packaging, which has become a bottleneck for producing high-performance processors. Industry spending on advanced packaging is forecast to approach $28 billion in 2026, Reuters reported.
ai.title: AI boom turns chip packaging into the next battleground for semiconductors

ai.summary: Investors’ concern that U.S. election results could lead to tighter rules or local resistance to data-center construction contributed to a steep selloff in AI-related stocks. The market reaction also reflected doubts about whether massive AI infrastructure spending will deliver sufficient returns.
ai.title: Nasdaq posts biggest daily drop in 19 months on fears of AI regulations

ai.summary: Potential investors in Anthropic’s planned IPO are questioning its expected valuation and whether it should proceed on its anticipated timetable, amid a technology-stock selloff. Reuters reported that investors are seeking a more attractive price and awaiting additional information about the company’s revenue.
ai.title: AI backlash could threaten Anthropic IPO timing, potential investors say

ai.summary: An independent assessment by METR found that Anthropic’s models have been improving on well-specified tasks roughly twice as fast as in the prior period, with AI assistance cited as a major contributor. The researchers cautioned that the estimate is uncertain and said AI had not yet made highly significant, fully autonomous contributions to key model-training stages.
ai.title: Anthropic's models improving nearly twice as fast with help from AI, study finds

ai.summary: A sharp retreat in AI-related shares spread into Asian markets, with chipmakers among the hardest hit. Reuters reported that concerns about data-center development and the financial returns on AI investment weighed on sentiment.
ai.title: Morning Bid: AI's reality check

ai.source: TechTimes, citing CNBC and Financial Times
ai.summary: Beijing-based Moonshot AI reportedly discussed leasing Nvidia Blackwell GPU capacity from European cloud operators, potentially in clusters of 8,000 or more GPUs. The report also describes proposed customer-allocation requirements for some new data-center contracts, though the article notes that renting chips abroad is legal under current U.S. rules.
ai.title: Moonshot AI Sought Nvidia Blackwell Rentals in Europe; Reported 51% Rule, Not US Law, Hits Lessors

quantum.summary: IBM, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD launched a co-design platform that colocates IBM quantum processors—including the 120-qubit Nighthawk—with AMD-powered high-performance computing. The partners will use it to study quantum error correction, decoding and the software workflows needed to connect quantum and classical systems.
quantum.title: AMD joins IBM and ORNL to advance quantum computing

quantum.summary: Quantinuum outlined a Nexus software roadmap intended to automate more of the process of encoding, compiling and running error-corrected quantum programs. The company says successive releases will add capabilities through its planned Apollo fault-tolerant system, targeted for 2029.
quantum.title: Quantinuum Unveils Nexus Roadmap

quantum.summary: Researchers reported a hybrid quantum-simulation framework combining superconducting qubits and microwave cavities to model interacting fermions and bosons. By encoding bosonic modes directly, the approach may reduce overhead for some simulations; the report describes it as a potential route for certain problems that does not rely on conventional error-correction overhead.
quantum.title: Hybrid Quantum Processors Sidestep Error Correction For Some Problems

quantum.summary: A team led by researchers at the Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology demonstrated a 97-nanosecond controlled-Z gate using the Autler–Townes effect. The reported fidelity was 99.40%, with static decoherence identified as the main source of remaining error.
quantum.title: A 97-nanosecond Gate Could Help Scale Up Superconducting Qubits

quantum.summary: IQM reported third-quarter revenue of €8.9 million, up 51% year over year, and an order backlog of €102.5 million. The company also highlighted orders including its Halocene system for the LUMI-IQ project, which is intended to support work toward logical qubits.
quantum.title: Finland’s IQM Posts 51% Q3 Revenue Climb, EUR 8.9 Million With Quantum Gains

quantum.summary: TU Delft researchers tested quantum lattice-Boltzmann fluid-dynamics algorithms on QuTech’s Tuna-9 and Tuna-17 processors through the Quantum Inspire platform. The small-scale experiments exposed accuracy degradation as circuits grew, underscoring the gap between current hardware and practical, large-scale computational-fluid-dynamics simulations.
quantum.title: Quantum Fluid Dynamics Codes Tested On QuTech's Tuna-9 And Tuna-17 Chips
